name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,779

indicatorNotes.review: to review something is to look it over again, going through it in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone is being told it is time to look again at the latest retirement payouts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Time' is prison slang for a sentence, as in 'doing time'; the pensions surface makes it look like the moment for a policy review.
annotation.definitionFit: Serving time means serving a prison sentence.

entries.clue: Yorkshire town favourite for celebrity promenade (3,6)

blocks.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire
a teacher's pet is the favourite

annotation.surface: A Yorkshire seaside town is tipped as the best spot for stars to parade.
annotation.walkthrough: Redcar is a seaside town on the North Yorkshire coast; the promenade in the surface sounds like its seafront.
annotation.definitionFit: The red carpet is the strip celebrities walk along at premieres.

indicatorNotes.scarpers: the student runs off, so the letter for a learner leaves the word

annotation.surface: A seasoned student runs off, content with what they have got.
annotation.walkthrough: L for learner, from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars, stands for a student; 'Seasoned' looks like it describes the student but is a word to work on.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone whose appetite has been fully met.

entries.clue: Chooses pub closing early, having no friends around (9)

indicatorNotes.closing early: the pub shuts before its end, so INN loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.around: friends standing around something surround it, so MATES encloses the IN

blocks.note: INN without its last letter, placed inside MATES

annotation.surface: Someone picks a pub that shuts early, since they have no friends there anyway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No mates' is British slang for a friendless loner, so the surface paints a lonely drinker; in the wordplay 'no' is kept literally and only the friends do the surrounding.
annotation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to choose or put them forward.

indicatorNotes.noisily: said out loud, so the answer is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: fed = ate, the past tense of eat, said out loud

annotation.surface: A rowing crew wolfs down its meal with lots of noise.
annotation.walkthrough: ATE and EIGHT sound identical, so the past tense of eat, spoken, becomes the number.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist sense: in rowing the boat and its crew are named after the number of oarsmen, as in the Boat Race between Oxford and Cambridge.

entries.clue: Write notes repeatedly about a private conversation (4-1-4)

indicatorNotes.repeatedly: the note is written again and again, four times over
indicatorNotes.about: the run of notes goes around A

blocks.note: TE is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, written four times
as printed, sitting in the middle

annotation.surface: Someone scribbles the same notes over and over about a quiet chat.
annotation.walkthrough: The notes are the sol-fa names (do, re, mi, fa, so, la, te); TE is the one used here.
annotation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête, French for head-to-head, is a private conversation between two people.

entries.clue: French city welcomes English family member (5)

indicatorNotes.welcomes: the city takes the E inside it

annotation.surface: A French city gives a warm reception to an English relative.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French city' tempts you to spell the whole answer in French; only the city is French, and the English letter goes into it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a brother's or sister's daughter is one of the relatives in a family.

indicatorNotes.doubled: the pair of letters is written twice

blocks.note: E (energy) + NT (National Trust), the whole written twice

annotation.surface: Energy-saving campaigners join forces to form a European agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: The National Trust (NT) is the British charity that conserves historic houses and countryside; 'doubled' applies to energy and conservationists together.
annotation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

indicatorNotes.blocks: the toilet sits inside the tax, plugging it

blocks.note: VAT, value added tax, split to hold the toilet
can is US slang for a toilet

annotation.surface: A lavatory is kept free of tax, or a tax-free toilet stands ready.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a toilet door, and the answer is the word on its lock indicator; 'blocks' reads like plumbing trouble but only tells one piece to sit inside the other.
annotation.definitionFit: Vacant means free, unoccupied, as a toilet sign says.

annotation.surface: A car is having its engine temperature checked at the garage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'check' sits at the end looking like part of the garage scene, but it is the definition, in its accountancy sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an inspection of a firm's accounts or records is a formal check on them.

indicatorNotes.lost: the eight letters have lost their way and come out jumbled
indicatorNotes.in: the jumbled word goes inside the fog

annotation.surface: The best rowing eight gets lost on the river in fog.
annotation.walkthrough: After 5 down, 'eight' again looks like a rowing crew; here it is only five letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, superlative matching superlative: most powerful of all.

blocks.note: a wedding ring is a band
if you are wearing something you have it on

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether to stop wearing their wedding ring.
annotation.walkthrough: Someone wearing a ring has 'a band on'; the question mark flags that the wordplay rearranges the order the clue gives.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to leave a plan or a place behind for good, which fits the surface's hint of walking out on a marriage.

entries.clue: Delaware taking part in school exchange (5-2)

indicatorNotes.taking part in: Delaware gets inside the school, becoming a part of it

blocks.note: to school someone is to train them
DE is the US postal abbreviation for the state of Delaware, placed inside TRAIN

annotation.surface: A Delaware school joins an exchange programme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun paired with exchange trips; it is the verb, meaning to train.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific kind of exchange: handing over an old car or phone as part-payment for a new one.

blocks.note: to tape something down secures it

annotation.surface: A group locks up its master recordings.
annotation.walkthrough: The same word does both jobs: a verb for fastening with sticky strip, and a plural noun for recordings on magnetic reel or cassette.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday: sticking something down fastens it, and bands once released their music on cassettes.

indicatorNotes.regenerated: the letters are made anew in another form

annotation.surface: A national park has restored a patch of green land.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly the sort of thing a national park does, which is why the fodder is easy to read past.
annotation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a national park in Tanzania famous for its wildlife migration.

entries.clue: Moderate hated being exposed as abstemious (9)

indicatorNotes.being exposed: the word is stripped of its outer covering, its first and last letters

blocks.note: to temper something is to moderate it
HATED without its outside letters H and D

annotation.surface: Someone's loathing of excess is revealed as sober self-restraint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like the definition, and TEMPERATE does mean moderate, but here it is only the verb giving TEMPER; the definition is 'abstemious'.
annotation.definitionFit: Temperate means restrained in eating and especially drinking, abstemious.

blocks.note: the M1, Britain's main motorway, with 1 read as I, plus 'S
a handle is a name or nickname

annotation.surface: Someone has got a road's name wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Yorkshire, and a crossword standard for 'road'; its digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in informal register: to botch a job by handling it badly.

entries.clue: Competitor of tech giant detailed international hypocrisy (9)

indicatorNotes.detailed: de-tailed: the word loses its tail, its last letter

annotation.surface: A rival of a big tech firm is accused in detail of global hypocrisy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Competitor of tech giant' reads as a rival company, but 'Competitor' alone is the definition and 'tech giant' goes to work as APPLE.
annotation.definitionFit: An applicant competes with others for a job or place.

entries.clue: Takes off bloomers, having posed at the outset (9)

indicatorNotes.at the outset: this piece comes at the start of the answer

blocks.note: a model who posed sat for the artist

annotation.surface: Someone strips off their bloomers after sitting for a painter.
annotation.walkthrough: Bloomers are old-fashioned baggy knickers, which is the surface's joke; in the wordplay they are flowers, things that bloom.
annotation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic and mock them, to satirise them.

entries.clue: Searched for company in certain difficulties initially (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the company goes inside the word for certain
indicatorNotes.initially: only the first letter of difficulties is used

annotation.surface: A firm in some trouble has been hunting around for a buyer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Searched for company' reads as one phrase; 'for' is only the link, and 'company' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: To scour a place is to search it thoroughly.

entries.clue: Discharge pollution initially in river and lake (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: only the first letter of pollution
indicatorNotes.in: that letter goes inside the river

blocks.note: the Exe, a river in Devon, opened as EX…E
first letter of pollution, placed inside EXE

annotation.surface: A factory's discharge leaks pollution into a river and lake.
annotation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England, a crossword regular because of its short letter pattern.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to force something out, as a body discharges waste or a pipe its effluent.

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing sizes
the adder is Britain's venomous snake

annotation.surface: Someone flees from a big snake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a verb for fleeing the snake; it is the British noun for a run in tights or stockings, a ladder.
annotation.definitionFit: A ladder is a run of unravelled stitches in tights.

entries.clue: Deep sea carbon in a green revolution (7)

indicatorNotes.revolution: a revolution turns the whole string round

annotation.surface: Carbon captured in the deep sea is part of a green revolution.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like it puts carbon inside something, but it simply gives the letters IN; the whole string C-IN-A-ECO then reads backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective for the open ocean far from shore, as in oceanic trenches, which is where the deep sea lies.
annotation.definitionNote: 'Deep sea' used adjectivally, as in 'deep-sea creatures'.

indicatorNotes.internally: the answer is found inside the words

annotation.surface: Financial matters are put in writing for internal use only.
annotation.walkthrough: 'internally' reads like office jargon for in-house paperwork; here it points inside the two words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: To endow something is to finance it with a gift of money.

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are put in a poor order

annotation.surface: A trainee misbehaved.
annotation.walkthrough: A short clue where the anagram fodder sits right beside its indicator; the only hurdle is seeing 'acted' as letters rather than a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee in the armed forces or police.

blocks.note: an app is a piece of software

annotation.surface: Useful software was sold on false claims.
annotation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' looks like an anagram indicator for 'software'; it is a plain word for having told lies.
annotation.definitionFit: Applied science is practical, put to use rather than theoretical.

indicatorNotes.enters: the Scotsman goes into the Post Office

blocks.note: PO = Post Office, opened as P…O
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

annotation.surface: A Scotsman slips into the Post Office without a sound.
annotation.walkthrough: Piano is the musical instruction to play softly; the surface makes 'quietly' describe how the man enters.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical direction: the Italian marking p on a score tells the player to play softly.

entries.clue: Ginger nut consumed by Morning Star journalist? (3-6)

indicatorNotes.consumed by: the nut is swallowed up inside the other letters

blocks.note: the Morning Star is a British communist daily, so its journalist is a RED; ED = editor, a journalist
nut is slang for head, placed inside RED ED

annotation.surface: A ginger biscuit gets eaten by a writer on a left-wing newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ginger nut' reads as the British biscuit; split it, and 'Ginger' is the definition while 'nut' means head.
annotation.definitionFit: Ginger hair is red hair, so a ginger person is red-headed.

blocks.note: AD, short for advertisement, standing for advertising

annotation.surface: A slogan is presented as the defining phrase of the advertising age.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'advertising era' is split into its two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a byword is a well-known saying, and an old proverb is the same thing.

blocks.note: someone spitting out feathers literally has down (soft feathers) in the mouth

annotation.surface: Someone is both low-spirited and furious, spitting feathers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spitting feathers' is British slang for being very angry or very thirsty; the clue reads it literally, with down as the fine feathers of a bird.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from the downturned mouth of a sad face, and literally a bird's soft down being spat out.
